_comment: Recommended allowlist: suppresses ONLY class-(c) schema noise — error classes empirically confirmed to occur identically in PRISTINE OpenStax sources (books/*/01-source/), i.e. defects in the schema or in upstream content, never introduced by our pipeline. Evidence: FINDINGS.md §2. Every rule states what it hides and what it could mask.

rules.reason: CNXML 0.7 binds abstract content to `common-attributes-noclass` (cnxml-defs.rng:933-945), which permits only xml:lang and data-platform-hidden — no @id. But OpenStax's own content generator stamps auto-generated ids (para-00001, list-00001) onto every <para>/<list>/<item> inside <md:abstract>. Affects 660 of 1192 pristine source files across all five books; identical count on both sides of every paired run. Nothing our pipeline does.
rules.risk: Narrow by construction: the expected-attribute list begins with data-platform-hidden ONLY in the no-class/no-id context, which in practice is the abstract. A body element rejecting @id would list "class", "data-platform-hidden", "id" and would NOT be suppressed. Re-verify if OpenStax changes the abstract content model.

rules.reason: RELAX NG authoring bug on the poet-schema branch: cnxml-defs.rng:935-944 wraps TWO <attribute> elements in a single <optional>, which makes them CO-REQUIRED rather than independently optional. Any element carrying xml:lang without data-platform-hidden is therefore rejected. Present in pristine orverufraedi (m58781, <foreign xml:lang="ar">). Absent on the master branch, which has no data-platform-hidden at all. Worth reporting upstream.
rules.risk: Hides a genuinely missing data-platform-hidden attribute — harmless, since that attribute is a platform hint we never author.

rules.reason: Upstream authoring defect in a legacy CNX physics module: <equation> in m42103 mixes literal text ('(a)At') with <m:math>/<sup>, which CNXML 0.7's equation content model disallows. Present in the pristine source; not something we introduced. Deliberately scoped to that one file rather than suppressing the message class globally.
rules.match: not allowed here; expected the element end-tag or text
rules.risk: Scoped to a single upstream file, so it cannot mask anything in our output. Drop this rule if that module is ever re-sourced.
